provenance.how: constructed from the ADR's literals at the pinned ref and cross-checked against the core's own builders (tests/unit/mobile/test_push_wire_contract.py); not captured from a running relay, because no relay route emits the machine-side shapes yet

forbidden.name: never a CONVERSATION name — not in the title, not in the body, not in any field (P2). The machine's own privacy flag gates LOCAL notifications only and is not a cloud-facing consent. (A device row's ``name`` in registry-list-response.json is the app's own label for a phone: a different field on a different shape, which is why this list is scoped to the payloads — see applies_to.)
forbidden.title: the banner's title is the cloud's house constant, not a machine field; sending one would carry a name by another spelling
forbidden.body: same rule: never composed from model output or a transcript snippet
forbidden.snippet: never sent; the desktop composer's body is a last-assistant-line snippet
forbidden.error: failure text may name a provider, a model or a quota — the refusal bodies on the relay's own routes are a different concern and are not usages of this list
forbidden.cwd: no working directory, no file path
forbidden.session_id: no raw session id: the conversation HANDLE is the wire identity, and the app resolves it on its own machine
forbidden.token: no push token — the machine validates and drops it, and the cloud's registry is where tokens live
forbidden.device_key: never on a list or an emit: the register response that mints it is its only carrier
forbidden.install_id: the app's identity, not the wire's
forbidden.operator_key: the machine's own secret, and the tunnel gateway cannot carry it
forbidden.badge: aps.badge is never sent, ever — the app owns the badge and corrects it by reading the machine's count
forbidden.aps: the machine sends the data object and stops; the envelope is the cloud's fan-out and a proposal
forbidden.revision: dropped: the badge comes from a read, not from a push, and revision counters leak activity volume
forbidden.count_completion: not a field name; listed so a reader does not read 'count' as a revision counter — count is the disclosed unread aggregate

notes: SCOPED TO THE PAYLOADS, not to every file in this tree: the list response is a relay response whose own forbidden array (registry-list-response.json) names its secrets, and it legitimately carries a device ``name`` — the label for a phone, never a conversation.
One home for the payload deny list, referenced by each emit shape, so a field is either allowed by the shape block or forbidden here — never both.
The cloud's contract is extra="forbid", so an unlisted field is refused rather than ignored; this file is the machine-side twin of that rule.
